name: Attai
overview: Attai was a male member of the tribe of Gad known for being the sixth Gadite to join David at Ziklag. His role is noted specifically in the context of those who came to support David during a critical time in his leadership, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:11. This highlights his participation among the Gadite warriors who aligned with David.
namesAndTitles: The name Attai means 'timely' or may be an abbreviation of Athaiah. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God, but it reflects a meaningful Hebrew name recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:11.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Attai as a descendant of Gad, linking him to one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Attai's significance lies in his role as one of the Gadite warriors who came to David at Ziklag, demonstrating the growing support for David among the tribes of Israel. Being the sixth Gadite to join David highlights the organized and willing allegiance that contributed to David's consolidation of power. His presence at Ziklag marks a moment when David's leadership was gaining acceptance among diverse Israelite groups.
